name: Button
description: A clickable button component with variants for different visual styles and sizes
designIntent: The Button component is a fundamental interactive element that triggers actions or navigation. It provides visual feedback through hover/active states and supports multiple variants to match different semantic contexts (primary actions, destructive actions, navigation, etc.).

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual style variant of the button

props.name: asChild
props.description: When true, renders as a child component using Radix Slot for composition

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the button and prevents interaction

props.name: children
props.description: Content to display inside the button

props.name: onClick
props.description: Handler called when button is clicked

examples.title: Primary action button
examples.description: Default variant for primary actions in the interface

examples.title: Destructive action
examples.description: Use for destructive or dangerous actions like delete, remove, etc.

examples.title: Outline button
examples.description: Secondary action with less visual weight

examples.title: As link
examples.description: Button styled as a link, using asChild for composition

antiPatterns.title: Don't use for navigation alone
antiPatterns.explanation: Buttons should trigger actions, not just navigate. Use proper navigation components.

antiPatterns.title: Don't nest buttons
antiPatterns.explanation: Never nest buttons - it breaks accessibility and HTML validity
antiPatterns.example:
// Avoid: Nested buttons are invalid HTML
<Button><Button>Click</Button></Button>

antiPatterns.title: Don't use vague text
antiPatterns.explanation: Button text should clearly describe what will happen

accessibility.implementation: Button is natively focusable and can be activated with Enter or Space key
accessibility.userRequirements: Ensure buttons have visible focus indicators

accessibility.implementation: Button role is automatically announced. Content is read as button label
accessibility.userRequirements: For icon-only buttons, add aria-label attribute

accessibility.implementation: Disabled buttons are not focusable and screen readers announce as disabled
accessibility.userRequirements: Don't rely solely on visual disabled state - ensure keyboard users also cannot activate

guidelines: Use action verbs (Submit, Save, Delete, Cancel)
Keep text short and concise (1-3 words ideally)
Use title case for primary actions
Be specific about what will happen
Avoid generic terms like 'Click here' or 'OK'
Always provide aria-label for icon-only buttons
Label should describe the action, not the icon

compositionRules.relationship: Buttons can contain icons alongside text or as icon-only buttons
Buttons commonly trigger dialog open/close actions
